open_trace.label: Open Trace
open_trace.plainEnglish: A copper track is cracked, so current can't flow past the break. Like a cut wire.
open_trace.example: A cracked solder joint or scratched PCB trace stops power from reaching a component.

short_nets.label: Short Circuit
short_nets.plainEnglish: Two separate tracks are accidentally connected, letting current bypass normal components. Like two bare wires touching.
short_nets.example: A solder bridge connects 5V directly to ground or crosses two signal lines.

part_open.label: Part Open Circuit
part_open.plainEnglish: A component has blown or burned out internally, disconnecting its pins completely. Like a burned-out lightbulb.
part_open.example: A blown resistor or fused inductor leaves an open gap in the circuit.

part_short.label: Part Short Circuit
part_short.plainEnglish: A component has failed internally such that all its pins are shorted together.
part_short.example: A damaged capacitor breaks down internally and behaves like a solid wire.

reverse_polarity.label: Reverse Polarity
reverse_polarity.plainEnglish: A polarized component is installed backwards, swapping its positive and negative terminals.
reverse_polarity.example: An LED or electrolytic capacitor inserted back-to-front fails to turn on or burns out.

value_drift.label: Component Value Drift
value_drift.plainEnglish: A component's electrical value shifts far outside its nominal tolerance due to heat, age, or manufacturing defect.
value_drift.example: A 10k resistor drifts to 20k or 1k, upsetting the voltage divider ratio.

overvoltage.label: Overvoltage
overvoltage.plainEnglish: A power source supplies a higher voltage than the circuit was designed to tolerate.
overvoltage.example: Accidentally plugging a 12V supply into a 5V circuit or an unexpected power surge.

missing_ground.label: Missing Ground
missing_ground.plainEnglish: The ground reference connection is lost, leaving signals without a return path.
missing_ground.example: A disconnected ground wire or broken ground plane causes floating signals and unexpected behavior.
